findings.description: The database password is interpolated into EC2 user data and written to a local PHP configuration file. User data can be retrieved by processes with instance access and is commonly retained in provisioning/logging paths, increasing the risk of credential disclosure.

The RDS instance is configured with publicly_accessible = true, assigning it a public network endpoint. Although the shown security-group ingress is VPC-scoped, this unnecessarily exposes the database to internet-reachable network paths and increases attack surface.
storage_encrypted = false leaves database storage, backups, snapshots, and replicas unencrypted at rest by default, exposing data if underlying storage artifacts are accessed.

The EC2 application role grants unrestricted s3:*, ec2:*, and rds:* actions against every resource. Compromise of the application instance would permit broad privilege abuse and access to resources beyond those required by the application.

MySQL port 3306 is allowed from the entire VPC CIDR rather than only the application security group or necessary hosts. Any compromised or unauthorized workload within the VPC can attempt to connect to the database.
